module purpose: neorv32_spi is a bus-controlled SPI block that stores control settings, accepts 9-bit transmit entries into a TX FIFO, shifts serial data through a transceiver into an RX FIFO, drives spi_clk_o/spi_dat_o/spi_csn_o and clkgen_en_o, and reports status and irq_o.

use-case flows.value: control-register settings written from the bus: enable, clock phase/polarity, prescaler/divider, highspeed mode, and interrupt-enable bits
a data-register write enqueues one 9-bit transmit entry into the TX FIFO
clock-generation and transceiver sequencing that fetches FIFO entries, updates chip select, shifts the serial byte, samples spi_dat_i, and marks transfer completion
status and interrupt reporting: RX/TX FIFO status, active chip-select state, busy state, and irq_o
a received byte returned on a data-register read after being written into the RX FIFO
control registers, interrupt output, transceiver state, chip-select outputs, and clock-divider state cleared by rstn_i; deasserting ctrl.enable also clears both FIFOs and resets the divider counter

conceptual assets.reasoning: The enable setting is stored by `ctrl.enable <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_en_c);` at line 140 and then directly controls whether both FIFOs are cleared (lines 211 and 243), whether interrupts may assert (line 255), whether the transceiver state machine is enabled through `rtx_engine.state(2) <= ctrl.enable;` (line 281), whether the divider counter is reset when disabled (lines 369-370), and what leaves on `clkgen_en_o` (line 383). Integrity is therefore established for configure and operate flows; availability is also established because the setting is held and returned on control readback at line 153, although the bus response port itself is transport-excluded.

conceptual assets.concept: SPI transfer timing and mode configuration
conceptual assets.reasoning: The stored phase, polarity, prescaler, divider, and highspeed settings are written at lines 141-145. The transceiver uses cpha/cpol to set and toggle the serial clock at lines 286, 301, 309, 320, 324, and 331, while the clock generator uses prsc/highspeed/cdiv to decide when `spi_clk_en` pulses at lines 371-377. Integrity is established because wrong settings change the implemented serial timing; availability is established because these registers retain their values and are returned on control readback at lines 154-158, with the transport readback port excluded from structural reporting.

The four interrupt-enable settings are written at lines 146-149 and consumed in the registered irq equation at lines 255-259. Integrity is established because the report flow requires irq_o to follow exactly the enabled RX-available, TX-empty, TX-not-half, and idle conditions; availability is established because these bits are retained and read back at lines 164-167, with the transport readback port excluded from structural reporting.

When a TX FIFO entry is a data byte, the transceiver loads `rtx_engine.sreg <= tx_fifo.rdata(7 downto 0);` at line 292 after the command/data test at line 289, drives the outgoing MSB on `spi_dat_o <= rtx_engine.sreg(7);` at line 343, samples `spi_dat_i` into `rtx_engine.sdi_sync` at line 310, and shifts that sampled bit back into `rtx_engine.sreg` at line 318. The completed byte is then forwarded to the RX FIFO by lines 244-245. Integrity is established because both the transmitted bit stream and the buffered received byte depend on this held byte; availability is established while enabled transfers advance on `spi_clk_en` at lines 299, 308, and 317. The persistent RX FIFO storage and bus readback path lie in a sub-unit or transport port, so the local references stop at the serial input, synchronizer, shift register, and serial output.

A TX FIFO command entry updates the chip-select control when `tx_fifo.rdata(8) = '1'` and `rtx_engine.cs_ctrl <= tx_fifo.rdata(3 downto 0);` at lines 289-290. The chip-select process then drives all outputs inactive and asserts one selected output low when `rtx_engine.cs_ctrl(3) = '1'` at lines 352-355. Integrity is established because the operate and report flows depend on the commanded external slave selection and the active-state readback at line 171; availability is established because the selected state is held until another command or the idle branch clears it at line 332.

The transceiver state register is updated by `rtx_engine.state(2) <= ctrl.enable;` at line 281 and the state-machine transitions at lines 293, 303, 312, 322, 325, and 333. This state decides when the TX FIFO is read (`tx_fifo.re <= '1' when (rtx_engine.state = "100") else '0';` at line 214) and is reduced to the busy decision by `rtx_engine.busy <= '0' when (rtx_engine.state(1 downto 0) = "00") else '1';` at line 340, which is then consumed for busy reporting and idle IRQ generation at lines 172 and 259. Integrity is established because operate and report flows depend on correct sequencing and busy/idle indication; availability is established because the state is held and advanced on clocked transfer steps.

conceptual assets.concept: FIFO availability status used for control and interrupts
conceptual assets.reasoning: `rx_fifo.avail` is reported at line 160 and used in the RX-available IRQ term at line 256. `tx_fifo.avail` is reported as TX-empty at line 161, contributes to the busy status at line 172, participates in the TX-empty and idle IRQ terms at lines 257 and 259, and decides whether the transceiver may consume a queued entry at line 288. `tx_fifo.half` is reported as TX-not-half at line 162 and used in the TX-not-half IRQ term at line 258. Integrity is established because these status decisions directly control operate and report behavior. `tx_fifo.free` only feeds transport readback at line 163 and is not locally tested here, so it is not listed as a structural reference under the sub-unit wiring rule.

The serial clock register is forced to the configured idle polarity at lines 286, 320, and 331, and takes the cpha/cpol-dependent active values at lines 301, 309, and 324 when `spi_clk_en` advances the transfer. `spi_clk_o <= rtx_engine.sck;` at line 344 then exports that value. Integrity is established because the operate flow and external serial timing depend on the exact clock level and edges; availability is established whenever enabled transfers and the clock generator produce clock-enable pulses.

The module computes `irq_o <= ctrl.enable and ((ctrl.irq_rx_avail and rx_fifo.avail) or (ctrl.irq_tx_empty and (not tx_fifo.avail)) or (ctrl.irq_tx_nhalf and (not tx_fifo.half)) or (ctrl.irq_idle and (not tx_fifo.avail) and (not rtx_engine.busy)));` at lines 255-259. Integrity is established because the report flow depends on that exact Boolean relation between configuration and status; availability is established because the output is registered each clock and reset to a known value at line 253.
